Author: Manju Rani Chauhan

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 49439 of 2019

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ravindra Prakash Srivastava

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Manju Rani Chauhan,J.

Heard Mr. Ravindra Prakash Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Mr. P.K. Sahi,
learned counsel for the State as well as perused the material on record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant-Ram Suresh Yadav Lal with a prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No. 141 of 2019, under Sections 272, 273, 419, 420, 467, 468, 471,
307, 504, 506, 332 I.P.C. and Sections 60, 60 (2), 63, 72 Excise Act and Section 7 of Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, Police Station-Pakoliya, District-Basti, during the pendency of the trial.

The first information report has been lodged on 7th October, 2019 by Sanjay Kumar, the then Station House Officer, Pakoliya Police Station against the four named accused persons including the present applicant with the allegation that on 6th October, 2019, when the informant and other Police personnels were checking the suspicious vehicles and miscreants to maintain law and order situation at Hasinabad Market/Crossing, one informer informed him that some people, who used to Ram Suresh Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 15 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77006026/
1 manufacture and sell illegal liquors, were standing at left side of road before Maheshganj Crossing and carrying drums of spirit in Bolero car and motorcycles and they were preparing to go somewhere. On believing the same

entities.text: Ram Suresh Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: , the informant and other Police personnels along with the officers of the Excise Department, after completing all legal formalities reached there and asked them to surrender.
Seeing the Police all the accused persons started firing upon the Police personnels, but they saved themselves and after surrounding them, they caught all the accused persons including the applicant.

37 plastic drums containing 2405 litres of spirit, 110 caps, 9765 rappers, 63 packets of vacant bottles, three mobile phone, Rs. 4050/- in cash, one country-made pistol of 315 bore, one used cartridge of 315 bore and one live cartridge of 315 are alleged to have been recovered from the spot.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
False and fabricated prosecution story has been made by the police.
The alleged recovery is planted one by the Police.
There is no independent or public witness from the basis of which it can be said that the applicant is involved in the commission of the alleged offence.
There is no chemical analysis report from which it can be said that the alleged recovered material is adulterated liquors.

It has further been argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been enacted by the legislature and hence the implication of the applicant under Sections 272, 273 I.P.C. is unjustified.
Offence under Section 60/63 of Excise Act is bailable and triable by the Magistrate.
Apart from the above, there is no injury case, therefore, no case punishable under Section 307 is made out against the applicant.
The applicant has no criminal antecedents to his credit except the present one.

It is next contended that there is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the witnesses and in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, the applicant shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
The applicant is in jail since 7th October, 2019.
Per contra learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant but he could not dispute the factual submissions as urged by the learned counsel for the applicant.

Considering the the nature of the offence, material/evidence brought on record, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties as well as the dictum of Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh Versus State of U.P. and another, reported in (2018) 3 SCC 22, let the applicant involved in aforesaid case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

sentences.text: (ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation

,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

It is clarified that the observations, if any, made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of the bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the ultimate merits of the case.

(Manju Rani Chauhan, J.) Order Date :- 15.11.2019 Sushil/-
